newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Twenty four journalists killed in Russia this year.
newsitem.headline: Twenty four journalists killed in Russia this year.

text.p: Twenty four journalists were killed in Russia and the rest of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) this year, bringing the toll to 130 since the Soviet Union fell apart, Itar-Tass new agency said on Wednesday.

Tass, quoting Oleg Panfilov, the head of the Glasnost Defence Fund that monitors human rights in the former Soviet Union, said they were print, television and radio journalists. They included foreigners and CIS citizens.
Many were killed in the breakaway region of Chechnya, where Russian troops spent 21 months trying to crush an independence bid.

Some were investigative journalists such as Russian crusading newspaper reporter Dmitry Kholodov, who had been probing possible mafia connections with Russia's military top brass and was killed in 1994 by a bomb aged 27.
Panfilov said journalists' rights were most at risk in Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Moldova and Kazakhstan.
The fund was named after the openness campaign of Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev before the collapse of the Soviet Union at the end of 1991.

The CIS, set up by Russian President Boris Yeltsin and his Ukrainian and Belarussian counterparts in December 1991, comprises 12 of the 15 former Soviet republics. The three Baltic states of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania refused to join.
